office: House Committee on Education and Labor (Democratic staff)
description:
The House Committee on Education and Labor (Democratic staff) seeks a Professional Staff member responsible for higher education issues such as accountability, accreditation, minority-serving institutions, and federal student loans.

Proficiency of programs authorized in the Higher Education Act is required.

Applicants should have two to four years of higher education policy or research experience or two years of higher education policy or research experience and an advanced degree.

This position is writing intensive and requires the ideal candidate to have exceptional writing, communication, and organizational skills. Must demonstrate the ability to successfully manage multiple projects under deadlines; display a collaborative disposition; and a commitment to social justice and expanding economic opportunity.
responsibilities: Leading a discrete number of higher education issue areas
Providing technical assistance to Member offices
Preparing written materials including talking points, letters, memos, and legislative analyses
Tracking regulatory developments, floor activity, and the related activities of other committees
Supporting the execution of committee preceedings and events related to higher education
Coordinating with the oversight and communications teams in support of the Committee’s agenda
qualifications: Two to four years of higher education policy or research experience or two years of higher education policy or research experience and an advanced degree
Exceptional writing, communication, and organizational skills
Ability to successfully manage multiple projects under deadlines
Commitment to social justice and expanding economic opportunity
how_to_apply: To apply, applicants must submit a resume and two short writing samples (no longer than 3 pages each) demonstrating a proficiency in higher education to E&L.Jobs@mail.house.gov with "Higher Education Professional Staff Position" in the subject line. Please apply no later than January 20, 2021.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, or sexual orientation. Candidates of diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply.
